sampling_model.design: An i.i.d. observational sample augmented by deterministic public nuisance functions \((m_0,m_1,p)\), supplied global \(L^2(P_X)\) error radii bounded by the fixed cap \(\bar r\), a fixed signal envelope \(E_P[(g_1(X)-g_0(X))^2]\le M\), and decision rules that may use all public inputs.
sampling_model.units: Independent units \(O_i=(Y_i,D_i,X_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), from a causal law satisfying consistency and conditional ignorability.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with propensity \(e(X)\), positive almost surely and allowed to approach zero.
sampling_model.overlap: Uniform one-sided dyadic shells satisfy \(c_-u^{\kappa}\le P\{u/2<e(X)\le u\}\le c_+u^{\kappa}\) for \(0<u\le\lambda_0\), while \(e(X)\le1-\eta_+\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The minimax infima range over rules measurable in \(O^{(n)}\) that also receive the supplied \(m_0\), \(m_1\), \(p\), \(r_{0n}\), \(r_{1n}\), and \(r_{en}\). The same public inputs are held fixed throughout each lower family, and the certified radii lie in \([0,\bar r]\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives the parametric-plus-nuisance-product structure-agnostic treatment-effect rate under a propensity bounded away from zero.
Section 2 gives the pure structure-agnostic ATE benchmark consisting of the parametric floor plus the nuisance-product rate under regular overlap.
Thresholded AIPW is uniformly asymptotically normal under sufficient weak-overlap nuisance conditions.
IPW has Gaussian or stable limits according to tail and trimming regimes.
Localized fuzzy hypotheses yield a minimax lower bound for pointwise CATE.
Inverse-weight estimation can have tail-dependent irregular rates.
Limited-overlap confidence accuracy is driven by local comparison-cell sizes.
Section 6.1 treats bounded-overlap ATE examples, while the conclusion identifies weak-overlap distribution shift as an open extension.

Theorem 3.1 gives asymptotic linearity and a studentized Gaussian limit for bias-corrected trimmed doubly robust estimators targeting the original treatment-effect estimand, with Proposition B.1 verifying the ATE specialization.

body.tldr: Global prediction accuracy does not determine the attainable accuracy of the population ATE once treated observations become polynomially rare. In a public-function experiment with fixed, bounded global \(L^2(P_X)\) certificates, a fixed \(L^2(P_X)\) envelope for the conditional treatment-effect signal, and uniform one-sided propensity shells, the proposed theorem identifies a four-channel frontier \(\rho_n\): tail-amplified outcome noise, regression error hidden in shells with no treated observations, localized propensity--treated-regression uncertainty, and the regular control-side nuisance interaction. The minimax decision class consists of measurable rules using the sample, public functions, and certified radii. A clipped doubly robust average attains absolute and fixed-probability risk, a five-block median attains root mean-squared risk, and a bias-aware interval has matching honest expected length. The open sequel asks for the exact cost of adapting to unknown shell and nuisance certificates.

project_justification.gap: Regular-overlap structure-agnostic theory gives a nuisance-product benchmark, while weak-overlap papers give trimming rules, irregular limits, or sufficient Wald conditions. MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026DRWeakOverlap, Theorem 3.1 and Proposition B.1, is especially close on target preservation: its bias-corrected trimmed doubly robust method retains the original ATE and yields asymptotic inference, but it does not characterize global-\(L^2\) public-function minimax risk or the matching lower bound for expected honest-set length. None of the opened papers jointly characterizes minimax absolute risk, root mean-squared risk, fixed-probability error, and expected honest-set length for the same full-population ATE under bounded global prediction-error certificates, a fixed conditional-effect signal envelope, an explicit public-information decision class, and uniform one-sided shells.
project_justification.niche: The public-function model separates what a learner knows globally from where treated observations actually occur. A fixed bound \(E_P[(g_1(X)-g_0(X))^2]\le M\) makes the ATE functional finite without imposing a pointwise or armwise outcome envelope. The left tail generates three treated-side obstructions with different scales, while the control-side product channel remains regular.
project_justification.fill: The core supplies an explicit public-information decision class, bounded nuisance radii, a fixed treatment-effect signal moment envelope, a single clipped estimator, a median amplification, four in-class converse channels whose regression amplitudes satisfy that envelope, the polynomial deterioration threshold, and an oracle bias-aware interval, all indexed by \(\rho_n\).

body.related_work: JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR, Theorem 1 and Remark 2, is the closest public-function experiment: it gives the doubly robust structure-agnostic rate when the propensity is bounded away from zero, and its asymmetric fuzzy hypotheses inform the dyadic-reservoir converse. BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE, Section 2, studies pure and smoothness-augmented black-box classes under regular overlap. The shell class is disjoint from the bounded-overlap public-function class, but Proposition 8 shows that its fast-tail rate limit retains \(r_{1n}/\sqrt n\) and is uniformly equivalent, under \(r_{1n}\le\bar r\), to their parametric-plus-product benchmark. JinSyrgkanis2025GeneralLinearFunctionalLowerBounds, Section 6.1 and the conclusion, broadens structure-agnostic lower bounds while retaining bounded-overlap ATE examples and expressly identifies weak-overlap distribution shift as open; it supplies the regime-opening anchor rather than a theorem matched here. Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics gives a clipped cross-fitted AIPW Gaussian limit under sufficient tail and nuisance conditions; it informs the upper score but is not a risk comparator. MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026DRWeakOverlap, Theorem 3.1 and Proposition B.1, constructs a bias-corrected trimmed doubly robust estimator that preserves the original ATE and establishes asymptotic linearity and normal inference; it does not give the global-\(L^2\) public-function minimax-risk frontier or the matching honest-length converse. MaWang2020RobustIPW derives Gaussian and stable IPW limits and selects a trimming threshold from the sample for its own IPW criterion; by contrast, the present oracle result fixes its threshold from the certified nuisance radii and targets full-population minimax risk. KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE provides the localized fuzzy-hypothesis method for a different estimand and smoothness class. KhanTamer2010Irregular explains why support tails govern inverse-weight rates. Rothe2017RobustCI motivates local effective sample size and limited-overlap coverage, but its robust intervals rely on finite-cell or auxiliary distributional structure rather than the four-channel global-\(L^2\) radius.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The lower frontier is restricted to reservoir-rich fixed shell constants satisfying ass:lower-shell-richness and ass:upper-shell-richness. Each lower family must also calibrate its regression perturbation to satisfy ass:bounded-treatment-effect-signal. The supplied constructions do so because the sole nonzero regression has \(L^2(P_X)\) norm within the relevant nuisance radius or a sufficiently small fixed constant. The upper bound needs only uniform shells and the fixed signal moment, so arbitrarily tight admissible shell constants may have a different converse geometry.
body.honest_scope: The main theorem treats supplied public functions, bounded certified radii, fixed shell constants, and the primitive signal condition \(E_P[(g_1(X)-g_0(X))^2]\le M\); it imposes no stronger pointwise or armwise potential-outcome envelope and makes no Wald or asymptotic-normality claim. The minimax rules may use every supplied public input. Adaptation to unknown calibration, bounded-outcome variants, arbitrary shell constants, and the exact studentized-validity region remain open. The dyadic-shell and bounded-overlap classes share the signal condition but are distinct; the fast-tail analytic limit is \((1+r_{1n})n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}+r_{0n}r_{en}\), which is uniformly equivalent to the known regular-overlap structure-agnostic rate under \(r_{1n}\le\bar r\).
